### Readings of the record

- `F4`, an interpretation of `F4F5-p108`, `F4-p26`, read by `case-author-1` and second reader `case-second-reader`: p.108 l.7 describes the July 17 transfer of $560 million of line costs to a Construction in Progress account, credited over three line cost accounts; p.26 l.5 gives an unsupported entry of exactly $560,000,000 on July 17, 2001. Read together they are one entry: the CIP debit is 560,000,000.00. The weaker reading, two different $560 million entries that day, has nothing in the record behind it. The split of the three credits is unsourced (a branch).
- `F12`, an interpretation of `F12F13-p116`, read by `case-author-1` and second reader `case-second-reader`: p.116 l.3 states the two 1Q02 entries in one sentence; F12 is the first, $718 million on April 12, reducing line cost expense and capitalizing it. F13 ($100 million on April 17) is W2's.
- `F1`, an interpretation of `F1-p106a`, `F1-p106b`, `F2-period`, read by `case-author-1` and second reader `case-second-reader`: p.106 l.3 states the instruction to reduce line costs by $771 million and increase two asset accounts by the total, $629 million into Other Long Term Assets and $142 million into Construction in Progress, and that the entries were booked on Friday, April 20; they sit under the report's first-quarter 2001 heading, so they adjust 2001Q1. "The entries" is plural: one entry or several is a branch.
- `F5`, an interpretation of `F4F5-p108`, read by `case-author-1` and second reader `case-second-reader`: p.108 l.7 states the two July 17 entries in one sentence; F5 is the second, $50 million of line costs moved into SG&A expenses, an expense-to-expense move.
- `F6`, an interpretation of `F6-p111`, `F6-p260`, `F6-p261`, `F9-period`, read by `case-author-1` and second reader `case-second-reader`: p.111 l.3 states the August 22 transfer of $544 million of the first quarter 2001 corporate adjustment out of Construction in Progress into an asset clearing account, cleared into ten assets of exactly $54.4 million each under the Fiber Optic Cable account; pp.260-261 (one sentence across the page break, held as two blocks) say the $544 million left the CIP accounts in 10 different entries of the same round-dollar amount. It sits under the report's third-quarter 2001 heading, so the entry is booked in 2001Q3. Its two intents are F6a (into clearing) and F6b (out to the ten items); one allocation or ten two-leg entries is the subledger_to_gl_legs reading.
- `F6-approval`, an interpretation of `F6-p111b`, read by `case-author-1` and second reader `case-second-reader`: p.111 l.3: the director rarely entered and approved entries himself, so his involvement in these transfers was unusual. The natural reading of the "so" clause is that he both entered and approved the August 22 transfers (self-approval). The weaker reading, that he only entered them, is the basis of W-P-01-CF-01.
- `F8`, an interpretation of `F8-p111a`, `F8-p111b`, `F8-p261`, `F9-period`, read by `case-author-1` and second reader `case-second-reader`: p.111 l.5 states the September 20 transfer of the 2Q01 adjustment of $560 million out of Construction in Progress into 12 assets, five totaling $250 million in Ocean Cable, three totaling $150 million in Computer Equipment and four totaling $160 million in Fiber Optic Cable; p.261 says the September 2001 transfer of the second quarter's $560 million was made as 12 entries in similar, round-dollar amounts. It sits under the report's third-quarter 2001 heading, so the entry is booked in 2001Q3. One entry or twelve is the entry_decomposition branch (one_entry / twelve_entries).
- `F10`, an interpretation of `F10-p114`, `F10-p114b`, `F10-period`, read by `case-author-1` and second reader `case-second-reader`: p.114 l.9 states that on January 23, 2002 a draft journal entry transferred $941 million from line cost expense to PP&E, and that the entry was made that same day into furniture and fixture accounts (plural; the split is unsourced); it sits under the report's fourth-quarter 2001 heading, so the entry adjusts 2001Q4 and is booked on 2002-01-23 (F10-p114's date).
- `F11`, an interpretation of `F11-p114`, `F11-p115`, `F10-period`, read by `case-author-1` and second reader `case-second-reader`: One sentence crosses the page break between p.114 and p.115, so the extraction holds it as two blocks: two days after F10, $100 million of the $941 million moved out of one of the asset accounts, offset by an accrual release from a general corporate accrual account; booked in 2001Q4 with F10.
- `F13`, an interpretation of `F12F13-p116`, read by `case-author-1` and second reader `case-second-reader`: p.116 l.3 states the two 1Q02 entries in one sentence; F13 is the second, $100 million on April 17, reducing line cost expense and capitalizing it.

| Attribute | Rule | Why |

| `approval_encoding` | `none` | the book posts each entry with no approval attached: an entry approval needs A0, and a draft promoted by its owner is W-P-01's own branch (plan §6.4) |
